mmi.walkthrough.title: Get started with MMI
mmi.walkthrough.description: Reference Excel/CSV tables from Markdown without copying them.
mmi.walkthrough.write.title: Write a reference with completion
mmi.walkthrough.write.description: Type `![[` in Markdown. Files, sheets, ranges (the tables on the chosen sheet) and options are offered with explanations.
mmi.walkthrough.author.title: Create or edit step by step
mmi.walkthrough.author.description:
Pick book, sheet, range and options, see what it renders as, then insert. On an existing reference only what you change is rewritten.

mmi.walkthrough.check.title: Check and fix references
mmi.walkthrough.check.description: Hover a reference to see what it renders as. Broken sheet or file names get fixes that list only existing targets.
mmi.walkthrough.paste.title: Turn an Excel copy into a reference
mmi.walkthrough.paste.description:
Copy cells in Excel, then run the command: the workspace books are searched for the same values and you pick where they came from.
[Insert Embed by Content Match](command:markdownMatrixInjector.insertEmbedByContentMatch)
mmi.setting.diagnosticsWhileTyping: While typing, hold back the diagnostics of the reference under the cursor (`quiet`, default) or show them at once (`full`). Opening, saving and moving to another line always report everything; the `mmi check` command and CI are always exhaustive.
mmi.setting.useClipboardSource: Local Windows only: when pasting an Excel copy with **Paste As** or *Insert Embed by Content Match*, read the copy source (book, sheet, cells) from the Windows clipboard with the built-in PowerShell and offer it first as "copy source confirmed" -- only after checking that the saved workbook shows exactly the copied values. Nothing is stored and nothing is inserted without your choice.
mmi.setting.semanticEnabled: **Experimental.** When a description of a table shares no word with any table name and nothing else matched, rank tables by meaning with a local embedding model (Ollama or an OpenAI-compatible server on this machine). Off by default. Needs a running runtime and a model you installed yourself; MMI never downloads one. Only book / sheet / title / header names and your request are sent, only to a loopback address. Results are inferred candidates that you choose; they can be wrong.
mmi.setting.semanticApi: Experimental. API of the local runtime: `ollama` (`/api/embed`) or `openai-compatible` (`/v1/embeddings`, e.g. LM Studio, llama.cpp server).
mmi.setting.semanticEndpoint: Experimental. Base URL of the local runtime. Only `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` and `::1` are accepted.
mmi.setting.semanticModel: Experimental. Embedding model already available in the local runtime. For Ollama / LM Studio, use **MMI: Select Existing Local Semantic Model** to choose one without downloading or loading models; other loopback OpenAI-compatible servers can still be configured manually.
mmi.setting.semanticMinScore: Experimental. Cosine similarity at or above which a table is offered. It depends on the model: measure with `scripts/cpu-search-eval/semantic-eval.ts` before relying on it.
mmi.setting.semanticQueryPrefix: Experimental. Prefix some embedding models need before a query (e.g. `query: ` for the e5 family).
mmi.setting.semanticDocumentPrefix: Experimental. Prefix some embedding models need before a document (e.g. `passage: ` for the e5 family).
mmi.setting.reviewObservation: Opt in to local Candidate-review observation. MMI appends session timing, selected-candidate count and review-state transitions to .mmi/candidate-review-observations.jsonl in the workspace. Candidate content and cell values are not recorded, and nothing is sent externally.
